items.title: Section: "One Mass, One Heap, One Mere Collection" — The Contemplation That Finally Achieves Transformation of Basis

items.zh: 復次，修觀行者，以阿賴耶識是一切戲論所攝諸行界故，略彼諸行，於阿賴耶識中，總為一團、一積、一聚。為一聚已，由緣真如境智修習、多修習故，而得轉依。轉依無間，當言已斷阿賴耶識。由此斷故，當言已斷一切雜染。
items.en:
Third, cultivation attention; first, clarifying the attainment of transformation. Furthermore, a practitioner of contemplation, recognising that the store-consciousness is the underlying cause of all conditioned phenomena subsumed under conceptual proliferation, gathers these phenomena together within the store-consciousness into a single mass, a single heap, and a mere collection. Having formed this collection, through cultivating, practising, and repeatedly cultivating wisdom taking suchness as its object, one achieves transformation of basis.
Second, concluding the severing of defilement. Immediately upon this transformation, the store-consciousness should be said to have been severed; by this severing, all defilement should be said to have been severed.

items.zh: 當知轉依，由相違故，能永對治阿賴耶識。

items.title: Section: "Since Beginningless Time, This Realm Is the Equal Basis of All" — Why the Store-Consciousness Establishes But Never Generates the Noble Path

items.zh: 又阿賴耶識體是無常，有取受性；轉依是常，無取受性，緣真如境聖道，方能轉依故。又阿賴耶識，恒為一切麁重所隨；轉依，究竟遠離一切所有麁重。又阿賴耶識是煩惱轉因，聖道不轉因；轉依是煩惱不轉因，聖道轉因。應知但是建立因性，非生因性。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing by latent afflictive tendency. Also, the store-consciousness is constantly followed by every coarse afflictive residue; transformation of basis has ultimately departed from all such residue.
Third, distinguishing by establishing cause; first, stating the distinction. Also, the store-consciousness is the cause for affliction's activity and the noble path's inactivity; transformation of basis is the cause for affliction's inactivity and the noble path's activity.
Second, explaining the nature of this cause. Know that this is only an establishing cause, never a generating cause.
Commentary: as the verse says, since beginningless time, this realm has been the equal basis of every phenomenon; by this, there are the destinies, and the attainment of nirvāṇa. The Establishment of Consciousness-Only Treatise explains: the verse's first half reveals the eighth consciousness's function as causal condition; its second half reveals its function as supporting basis for both saṃsāra's turning and its reversal.

items.title: Section: Bound in Every Wholesome Deed Until Transformed, Free in Every Wholesome Deed Once Transformed

items.zh: 又阿賴耶識，令於善、淨無記法中不得自在；轉依，令於一切善、淨無記法中得大自在。
items.en:
Fourth, distinguishing by obstruction and freedom. Also, the store-consciousness prevents freedom within wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena; transformation of basis grants great freedom within all wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena.
Commentary: as for preventing freedom within wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena — "pure-neutral" names what is uncovering yet neutral. While the store-consciousness remains defiled, the bondage of coarse affliction not yet departed prevents freedom within wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena; once transformation of basis is achieved, defilement severed, every coarse affliction utterly departed, complete freedom is attained within all wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena.

items.title: Section: "Merely Borrowed Time" — Living On After Liberation, and What Finally Ceases at Death

items.zh: 又阿賴耶識斷滅相者，謂由此識正斷滅故，捨二種取，其身雖住，猶如變化。所以者何？當來後有苦因斷故，便捨當來後有之取；於現法中一切煩惱因永斷故，便捨現法一切雜染所依之取。一切麁重永遠離故，唯有命緣暫時得住。由有此故，契經中言：爾時但受身邊際受、命邊際受。廣說乃至即於現法一切所受究竟滅盡。如是建立雜染根本故，趣入、通達、修習作意故，建立轉依故，當知建立阿賴耶識雜染還滅相。
items.en:
Second, the characteristics of the store-consciousness's own cessation; first, belonging to the Stage With Residue Remaining; first, stating. Also, as for the characteristics of the store-consciousness's own cessation, because this consciousness has genuinely ceased, two kinds of grasping are relinquished; though the body continues, it is as though an illusory transformation.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining; first, relinquishing two kinds of grasping. Because the cause of future suffering is severed, grasping towards future existence is relinquished; because every cause of present affliction is permanently severed, grasping towards the present basis of all defilement is relinquished.
Second, life's condition temporarily remaining; first, stating the reason. Because every coarse affliction has permanently departed, only the condition of remaining life keeps one temporarily abiding.
Second, citing scriptural proof. Because of this, scripture says: at that time, one experiences only feeling at the limit of the body and feeling at the limit of life.
Second, belonging to the Stage With No Residue Remaining. And so on at length, until, in this very life, all feeling comes to its own ultimate and complete cessation.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Through establishing the root of defilement, through entering, penetrating, and cultivating attention, and through establishing transformation of basis, one should understand the complete establishment of the store-consciousness's own turning of defilement and reversal.

items.zh: 如是已依勝義道理，建立心、意、識名義差別；由此道理，於三界等諸心、意、識，一切雜染、清淨道理，應隨決了。

items.title: Section: Four Ways of Having or Lacking the Store-Consciousness — The Entire Discussion's Elegant Capstone

items.zh: 餘處所顯心、意、識理，但隨所化有情差別，為嬰兒慧所化權說，方便令彼易得入故。問：若成就阿賴耶識，亦成就轉識耶？設成就轉識，亦成就阿賴耶識耶？答：應作四句。或有成就阿賴耶識，非轉識。謂無心睡眠、無心悶絕、入無想定、入滅盡定、生無想天。或有成就轉識，非阿賴耶識。謂阿羅漢、若諸獨覺、不退菩薩，及諸如來住有心位。或有俱成就。謂餘有情住有心位。或有俱不成就。謂阿羅漢、若諸獨覺、不退菩薩，及諸如來入滅盡定，處無餘依般涅槃界。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing this from other teachings. The principle of mind, manas, and consciousness shown elsewhere merely accords with the particular beings being transformed, provisionally taught for those of childlike wisdom to make entry easier for them.
Second, distinguishing possession; first, posing the question. Question: if one possesses the store-consciousness, does one also possess the active consciousnesses? If one possesses the active consciousnesses, does one also possess the store-consciousness?
Second, answering; first, stating the four alternatives. Answer: four alternatives should be given.
Second, explaining each individually; first, the first alternative. One may possess the store-consciousness without the active consciousnesses: as in dreamless sleep, fainting, the attainment without perception, the attainment of cessation, and rebirth in the heaven of no perception.
Second, the second alternative. One may possess the active consciousnesses without the store-consciousness: as with arhats, pratyekabuddhas, non-retrogressing bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas abiding in a state with active mental consciousness.
Third, the alternative of both. One may possess both together: as with all other beings abiding in a state with active mental consciousness.
Fourth, the alternative of neither. One may possess neither: as with arhats, pratyekabuddhas, non-retrogressing bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas entering the attainment of cessation, or entering the realm of nirvāṇa without residue remaining.

items.title: Section: A New Topic Opens — Why Fire Is Named for Its Fuel, and Consciousness for Its Faculty and Object

items.zh: 問：內外諸法自性各別，各住自相，何因緣故，十八界中唯六識界自性建立，所餘諸界為彼所依、所緣、助伴而建立耶？答：由六識界，於彼彼念瞬息、須臾、日夜等位速疾轉變，託彼彼緣，依眼等根，緣色等境，用諸心所以為助伴，非一眾多種種生起。由彼彼依之所生故，得彼彼名。如火依附彼彼緣故而得燒然，爾時便得彼彼名數。由諸草木、牛糞、糠札等為緣故，火方得然，爾時便數名為草火，乃至札火。如是眼、色以為緣故，眼識得生，數名眼識；如是乃至數名意識。
items.en:
Second, distinctions among the forms of consciousness; first, clarifying their establishment; first, posing the question. Question: among the inward and outward phenomena, each bearing its own distinct characteristic, why, among the eighteen elements, are only the six consciousness-elements established as bearing their own essential nature, while the remaining elements are established as their basis, object, or accompanying support?
Second, answering; first, distinguishing their differences; first, the six consciousness-elements; first, clarifying their arising. Answer: because the six consciousness-elements transform with great rapidity, moment by moment, over a fleeting instant, a brief while, or a full day and night, relying on this or that condition, depending on the eye and other faculties, taking form and other objects, using various mental factors as accompanying support, arising as countless, ever-varied instances.
Second, explaining how the name arises; first, presenting the basis; first, stating the principle overall. Because each arises in dependence on its own particular basis, it receives its own particular name — just as fire, depending on this or that condition, comes to burn, and is accordingly given this or that name.
Second, explaining the characteristic individually; first, presenting the simile. Because fire arises in dependence on grass, wood, cow-dung, or husks as its condition, it is accordingly called grass-fire, up through husk-fire.
Second, applying the simile. So too, in dependence on the eye and form as conditions, does eye-consciousness arise, accordingly called eye-consciousness; and so on up through mental consciousness.

items.title: Section: Six Faculties That Never Change, One Consciousness That Never Stops Changing — Establishing Identity Closes

items.zh: 餘眼等界，若彼自性從初生已，即彼自性相似生起，展轉相續，究竟隨轉。又一識類，藉彼彼緣，種種差別自性生起。是故識界自性建立，所餘諸界為彼所依、所緣、助伴而得建立。
items.en:
Second, the eye and other elements. As for the remaining elements such as the eye, from the very first moment of a life, they arise in a similar, continuous succession, continuing until the very end.
Third, a single class of consciousness. Also, this single class of consciousness, relying on this or that condition, gives rise to various distinctly differentiated natures of its own.
Second, concluding the establishment. Therefore identity is established through the consciousness-elements, while the remaining elements are established as their basis, their object, and their accompanying support.

blocks.text: The discussion of the store-consciousness ends with its transformation: what remains, and what ceases, when the basis is transformed.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the store-consciousness is the cause of all conditioned things; when it is severed, the name is dropped, not its clarity. (Untranslated, 0581c08: the transformation of the basis permanently counteracts the store-consciousness, since the two are opposed.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: the store-consciousness makes affliction active and the path inactive. It is an establishing cause of the path, a dominant condition, not a causal one; pure seeds merely lodge in it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: despite the sixth consciousness's effort, innate self-grasping leaves one unfree until the basis is transformed.

Both graspings gone, the body remains "as if an illusory transformation". Master Cháng Bǎi: life's conditions keep one here for now. (Untranslated, 0581c28: the distinction of mind, manas, and consciousness has now been set out according to the ultimate; all defilement and purity in the three realms should be understood by it.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: "active consciousnesses" here means the first six; ordinary beings have both kinds.
Consciousness transforms swiftly, arising in many ways. "Fire is named from its fuel": Master Cháng Bǎi, consciousness is named by its conditions. A 瞬息 is a blink; a 須臾 is forty-eight minutes.
Master Cháng Bǎi: from the start of a life, in the womb, the faculties continue similarly, unlike the six consciousnesses.
"As if an illusory transformation." The liberated person still lives, eats, and walks, but holds nothing of it as self.

quiz.q: "Realm" renders 界 here. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain, and what is "severed"?
options: 界 means cause of conditioned things; what is severed is the name, not its clarity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the cause of all conditioned things; severing drops the name, not its clarity. "Realm" hides this.

quiz.q: How do the two stand opposite as establishing causes?
options: the first causes affliction's activity and the path's inactivity; the second the reverse
quiz.why: They are exactly opposite. Master Cháng Bǎi: it makes affliction active and the path inactive.

quiz.q: The English uses "generating cause" for two different terms. How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate this consciousness to the path?
options: an establishing cause and dominant condition, not a generating cause; pure seeds merely lodge there
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is an establishing cause of the path, a dominant condition, not a causal one; pure seeds merely lodge in it.

quiz.q: "Prevents freedom within wholesome and pure-neutral phenomena." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: however hard the sixth does good, innate self-grasping keeps one in saṃsāra
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: despite the sixth's effort, innate self-grasping leaves one unfree.

quiz.q: After its cessation, how does the body continue?
options: two graspings relinquished; though the body continues, it is like an illusory transformation
quiz.why: Two graspings gone; the body remains as if an illusory transformation. Master Cháng Bǎi: life's conditions keep one here for now.

quiz.q: "Attain" renders 成就 in the four alternatives. Who has active consciousnesses without the store-consciousness?
options: arhats, pratyekabuddhas, non-retrogressing bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas with mind; 成就 means having, not attaining; "active" means the first six
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "active" here means the first six; ordinary beings have both. Since they already have it, "attain" doesn't fit 成就.

quiz.q: Why are only the six consciousness-elements established by their own nature?
options: they change swiftly, arising variously through conditions, faculties, and objects
quiz.why: They transform swiftly, arising in many ways. Master Cháng Bǎi: moment by moment, day and night.

quiz.q: Which simile shows how consciousness gets its name?
options: fire named grass-fire or husk-fire from its fuel
quiz.why: Fire named from its fuel. Master Cháng Bǎi: named by its conditions.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 瞬息 and 須臾?
options: a blink; one 須臾 is forty-eight minutes
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 瞬息 is a blink; 須臾 is forty-eight minutes. The English gives only the gist.

quiz.q: How do the eye and other elements differ from consciousness?
options: they arise similarly from life's start, unlike the swiftly changing six
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the start of a life, in the womb, they continue similarly, unlike the six.

quiz.q: What readings of "a single class of consciousness" does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: eight sharing cognition; one substance named by faculties; or moral differences within one consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: eight share cognition; or are one substance named by faculty; or one consciousness holds moral differences.
